summary: Iter67 growth/conversion package tested end-to-end (backend + frontend + share/reviews/discounts). Backend pytest: 10/13 PASS (3 failures are symptoms of a HIGH-priority environmental issue — the background conversion_loop in growth.py is running autonomously in the preview env and already fired REAL sweeps that (a) sent real Gmail emails to smtest.parent@example.com, (b) stamped conv_mail1/2/3_sent_at flags on all 3 seed reports, (c) stamped auto_48h discount on BOTH smtest-30h AND smtest-50h (drift), (d) marked txn smtest-txn-1 abandon_mail_sent_at, so future dry-run sweeps return 0 items and smtest-50h's discount is not null anymore. The sweep endpoint / discount / campaign / share / reviews code paths themselves are correct — only the background loop is unsafe for a preview DB). Frontend: all owner flows PASS (discount-banner + paywall-discount-chip + smt-bonus-card on /report/smtest-30h; full share flow on /report/smtest-80h — pill→modal→img→copy-btn→POST /share-unlock 200→success state→bonus card appears→pill disappears; /s/{token} logged-out public teaser renders with story+CTA; landing reviews-strip visible; dashboard review-prompt renders and lets user edit). One HIGH-priority frontend bug found: Admin Reviews tab crashes with runtime error 'destroy is not a function' and renders 0 review items — root cause is `useEffect(load, [])` where `load` returns a Promise (same anti-pattern in GrowthAdmin.jsx:20). Admin Growth tab: auto-percent input + dry-run button + campaign name input all render; dry-run returns JSON (currently empty due to background loop drift); campaign-percent input has no data-testid so it wasn't detected by that selector.

critical.issue: Background asyncio loop calls conversion_sweep(dry_run=False) every 15 minutes on server startup — actively sends real Gmail emails and mutates the DB (sets conv_mail*_sent_at flags, stamps discounts). In a preview environment with seeded test data this defeats the review-request's explicit 'do NOT send real emails' constraint and makes repeatable dry-run testing impossible (all seed reports now have the sent flags). Recommend guarding the loop behind an ENV flag (e.g. ENABLE_GROWTH_LOOP=1) that is OFF in preview.

minor.issue: Cannot reproduce '4 planned items' expectation because sent-flags were already mutated by the background loop before testing began. Returns []. Code path itself looks correct in growth.py.

Expected pricing.discount = null. Actual: auto_48h 25% discount is present, because background sweep stamped it 50h into the seed's lifetime. Not a code bug — direct consequence of the above HIGH issue.

ui_bugs.issue: Uncaught TypeError: 'destroy is not a function'. Line `useEffect(load, [])` where `load = () => api.get(...).then(...).catch(...)` returns a Promise, which React tries to call as cleanup. Reviews tab shows 0 items despite backend returning them, and any tab-switch surfaces the runtime error overlay. Fix: `useEffect(() => { load(); }, []);` in both files.

issues: Campaign 'percent' input is missing data-testid='campaign-percent' (the name input has one). Add for testability.

action_items: HIGH: Guard growth.py conversion_loop() behind an ENV flag (e.g. ENABLE_GROWTH_LOOP) OFF by default in preview so it does not auto-send real emails / mutate seeded test data.

HIGH: Fix `useEffect(load, [])` in /app/frontend/src/components/admin/ReviewsAdmin.jsx:16 and /app/frontend/src/components/admin/GrowthAdmin.jsx:20 — change to `useEffect(() => { load(); }, []);` to stop React from treating the returned Promise as a cleanup fn. This unblocks the Admin Reviews tab (currently crashing/empty).

rca of the issue: Two independent root causes: (1) growth.py:185 spawns `conversion_loop` on startup with no env gate; it calls conversion_sweep with dry_run=False every 15 min → real SMTP + DB mutation. (2) ReviewsAdmin.jsx:16 and GrowthAdmin.jsx:20 use `useEffect(load, [])` where `load` is an arrow that returns `api.get(...).then(...)` (a Promise). React sees the effect callback return non-undefined and expects it to be a cleanup fn → 'destroy is not a function' TypeError on unmount, corrupting the tab render and leaving items=[]. Fix is a one-line wrap in both files.
